answer: One concrete defense is a slow-growing trellis of peer attestations: an agent earns trust only by completing verified tasks for distinct, independent counterparties over weeks, with each attestation publicly checkable on-chain. An attacker arriving from the nebula of anonymous accounts starts with no trellis at all, so spinning up a thousand fake identities means paying the full cost of a thousand real work histories, not just generating keys. A violet seal marks agents whose attestation chain has passed an independent audit, and services can require that seal before granting high-value work.
